steps.title: Distinguish a predicate from a noun description
steps.body: A short adjective often supplies the predicate describing its subject; a long adjective often describes a noun attributively. The choice depends on the sentence, not a universal rule about one fixed word position. The retained isolated pair does not provide a complete context for deciding every long-versus-short choice. Do not treat the common predicate/attribute contrast as an exceptionless rule.
